title: Andaman
tagline: Turquoise water, white sand and coral reefs
description: Scattered across the Bay of Bengal, the Andaman Islands are India's most beautiful escape to the sea. Powder-white beaches meet water so clear you can see the coral from the boat, and rainforest runs right down to the shore.

Base yourself in Port Blair to explore the islands' history at the Cellular Jail and Ross Island, then take the ferry to Havelock for Radhanagar Beach — regularly ranked among Asia's finest — and some of the country's best snorkelling and diving.

highlights.title: Radhanagar Beach, Havelock
highlights.text: A sweeping arc of white sand backed by forest — one of Asia's most celebrated beaches, perfect at sunset.

highlights.title: Cellular Jail Light & Sound Show
highlights.text: Walk the corridors of the historic 'Kala Pani' prison, then watch its freedom-struggle story told in light and sound.

highlights.title: Ross Island & North Bay
highlights.text: Explore the ruins of the British-era capital reclaimed by banyan trees, then snorkel among the corals of North Bay.

highlights.title: Scuba diving & snorkelling
highlights.text: Discover vibrant reefs, sea turtles and tropical fish at Havelock and Neil Island — beginner dives need no experience.

highlights.title: Elephant Beach
highlights.text: A short boat ride from Havelock to clear shallows for snorkelling, glass-bottom boat rides and sea walking.

highlights.title: Natural Bridge, Neil Island
highlights.text: A rock arch carved by the sea, revealed at low tide along with rock pools full of corals and starfish.

highlights.title: Sunset at Chidiya Tapu
highlights.text: Watch the sun sink into the sea from the southern tip of South Andaman, a haven for birdwatchers.

highlights.title: Baratang's limestone caves
highlights.text: Cruise through mangrove creeks to walk among ancient limestone formations deep in the forest.
